title: World-R1: Reinforcing 3D Constraints for Text-to-Video Generation
claim: Our method turns plain text prompts into high-quality videos whose frames are geometrically consistent enough to reconstruct as 3D worlds.
layout: 4 rows by 5 columns: prompt, three frames, 3D reconstruction in dashed box
description: A gallery with four rows, each showing one example. The left column gives a text prompt with a camera instruction, for example 'Camera push in' followed by a scene description: an industrial game world, an afternoon tea set, liquid metal spheres over a lake, and a glowing mushroom forest. Three wide video frames per row follow, showing the camera moving through the scene. The rightmost column sits in a dashed rounded box labeled '3D World Visualization'. It shows a point-cloud reconstruction of each scene with a rainbow camera trajectory. Bold column labels at the bottom read Text Prompt, Generated Video and 3D World Visualization. The eye goes first to the vivid frames, then to the dashed 3D column.
caption: World-R1 enables geometrically consistent world modeling in video foundation models via reinforcement learning. It accepts text input and generates high-quality 3D consistent videos. We visualize the reconstruction results alongside the video frames. Video results are in our supplementary material.
abstract: Recent video foundation models demonstrate impressive visual synthesis but frequently suffer from geometric inconsistencies. While existing methods attempt to inject 3D priors via architectural modifications, they often incur high computational costs and limit scalability. We propose World-R1, a framework that aligns video generation with 3D constraints through reinforcement learning. To facilitate this alignment, we introduce a specialized pure text dataset tailored for world simulation. Utilizing Flow-GRPO, we optimize the model using feedback from pre-trained 3D foundation models and vision-language models to enforce structural coherence without altering the underlying architecture. We further employ a periodic decoupled training strategy to balance rigid geometric consistency with dynamic scene fluidity. Extensive evaluations reveal that our approach significantly enhances 3D consistency while preserving the original visual quality of the foundation model, effectively bridging the gap between video generation and scalable world simulation.
